primary_judgments.case: Reidy v The Governor and Company of Bank of Ireland [2023] IECA 212
Fannon v Ulster Bank Ireland DAC [2024] IECA 51
primary_judgments.role: limits of s.31 as evidence of underlying transfer/assignment terms

primary_judgments.case: Planetwhite Ltd v Hogan & Anor [2025] IEHC 378
primary_judgments.role: registered owner not in possession; s.31 and statutory burdens

verified_propositions: Section 31(1) gives the register the statutory conclusive effect specified by the Act, subject to the statutory exceptions and rectification framework.
The statutory conclusiveness is not confined by its text to an owner who is physically in possession; Planetwhite applied it to a registered owner seeking possession.
Section 31 does not make the register conclusive evidence of every term of an underlying transfer or assignment; Fannon is material to that evidential distinction.
The 'iron curtain' / curative-effect description comes from the judicial treatment of registered title and must be presented as judicial characterization, not as statutory wording.
Overriding-interest questions and existing legal rights of occupation remain separate from the conclusiveness of the registered title.
limits: The proposition does not establish the facts of an individual property.
Fraud/mistake and statutory rectification routes remain material.
Boundary/map questions remain governed by their separate statutory and evidential framework.
This audit does not determine any future court outcome.
remaining: Final publication-source audit and separate boundary/possessory-title gaps.
